title: Impossible Differential Beyond Four Steps for Trax-M
summary: Trax-M has a known four-step impossible differential, but it remains unresolved whether any impossible differential can span more than four steps.

formal_statement.body: For Trax-M, Alzette is applied to both branches in each round, so the usual five-round Feistel impossible-differential pattern does not apply. The best identified impossible differential spans four steps: for any nonzero 64-bit differences $\delta$ and $\Delta$, $\Pr[(0,\delta)\to(\Delta,\Delta)]=0$. Determine whether Trax-M admits an impossible differential spanning more than four steps; either construct one or prove that no such longer impossible differential exists under this round structure.

scope.domain: Differential cryptanalysis of the Trax-M block-cipher construction, focusing on impossible differentials in its two-branch Alzette round structure.
parameters: Trax-M: target construction and round structure
four steps: span of the best identified impossible differential
nonzero 64-bit differences delta and Delta: difference values in the transition
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether Trax-M admits an impossible differential spanning more than four steps, either by constructing one or proving that no such longer impossible differential exists under this round structure.

citations.label: Alzette: a 64-bit ARX-box (feat. CRAX and TRAX)

progress.summary: The source reports a four-step impossible differential as the best one it found after noting that the standard five-round Feistel pattern does not apply because Alzette acts on both branches. It leaves longer impossible differentials unresolved.
